items.title: Hilbert tensor construction
items.statement: For complex Hilbert spaces H,K, the algebraic tensor product H⊙K carries the sesquilinear form induced by the two pairings; the form is a genuine inner product, its completion H⊗̂K is a complex Hilbert space in which the elementary tensors u⊗v have norm ‖u‖‖v‖, orthonormal families with dense span in H and K produce an orthonormal family with dense span in H⊗̂K, and finite sums have a unique orthonormal-coordinate expansion with squared norm Σ|c_ab|².
items.strategy: Prove the C-vector-space structure and well-definedness of the pairing on the quotient, positive definiteness by orthonormal coordinates of the finite-dimensional factor spans, then complete and extend the product-basis density by the norm estimate ‖u⊗v−u'⊗v'‖≤‖u−u'‖‖v‖+‖u'‖‖v−v'‖.

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, §1.4 pp. 45-47 (tensor construction)
MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 8 'Multiparticle States and Tensor Products', PDF pp. 1-12

items.title: Rank-one operator calculus
items.reference: local prerequisite added by batch-35 scaffolding (published rank-one trace facts were previously cited through a B-page example)
items.statement: For a complex Hilbert space H and u,v in H, T_{u,v}x=<x,v>u is bounded with norm ||u||||v||, trace class with trace norm ||u||||v|| and trace <u,v>, has adjoint T_{v,u}, is positive for u=v with trace ||x||^2, multiplies as BT_{u,v}=T_{Bu,v}, T_{u,v}B=T_{u,B*v} for bounded B, satisfies tr(ST_{x,y})=<Sx,y>=tr(T_{x,y}S) for trace-class S, and the map (u,v)->T_{u,v} is trace-norm continuous.
items.strategy: Finite-rank membership and the one-term nuclear representation give the trace-class property, trace norm and trace; the adjoint, positivity and product identities are direct pairing computations; continuity follows from bilinearity and the trace-norm triangle inequality.

references.title: A. W. Knapp, Advanced Real Analysis, Chapter II §5 (rank-one operators, trace class and the trace norm)
G. Teschl, Topics in Real and Functional Analysis (2019), §3.6 pp. 97-104 (Hilbert-Schmidt and trace class operators)

items.title: Bounded tensor maps
items.statement: Bounded operators S∈B(H,H'), T∈B(K,K') have a unique bounded tensor extension S⊗T on H⊗̂K with (S⊗T)(u⊗v)=Su⊗Tv and ‖S⊗T‖≤‖S‖‖T‖; the adjoint is S*⊗T*, composition multiplies, and S⊗I, I⊗T commute. No assertion is made for unbounded maps.
items.strategy: Define S⊗T on elementary tensors, estimate ‖(S⊗I)z‖ and ‖(I⊗T)z‖ in orthonormal coordinates, extend by density and bounded extension, then transfer adjoint, product and commutation identities from the dense elementary tensors.

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, §1.4 pp. 45-47 (tensor product of operators)
MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 8 'Multiparticle States and Tensor Products', PDF pp. 1-12

items.title: Density and scalar spectral probability
items.statement: A density operator on a nonzero separable complex Hilbert space is a positive self-adjoint trace-class operator of trace one; it admits trace-norm convergent spectral expansions ρ=Σ w_n T_{u_n,u_n} with orthonormal u_n and weights w_n≥0 summing to one, and every such weighted sum is again a density operator. For every PVM E the set function μ_ρ(B)=tr(ρE(B)) is a probability measure with μ_ρ(B)=Σ w_n‖E(B)u_n‖², reducing to μ_ρ(B)=‖E(B)u‖² for pure ρ=T_{u,u}; under the additional Axiom of Choice the scalar spectral law of a self-adjoint A has mean ⟨Aψ,ψ⟩ and second moment ‖Aψ‖² for unit ψ∈D(A).
items.strategy: Use the compact spectral theorem and trace-class ideal/nuclear estimates for the decomposition and its convergence, test the trace pairing against bounded projections for σ-additivity of μ_ρ, and obtain the moment clauses from the PVM form of the unbounded spectral theorem (choosing the domain where the moment integrals converge).

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Ch. 2-3 pp. 55-100 (adjoints, spectral theorem, scalar spectral measures)
J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, §6.3 pp. 121-128 (density operators)

items.title: Weak-form Robertson uncertainty
items.statement: For self-adjoint A,B and a unit vector u∈D(A)∩D(B), the preparation standard deviations satisfy ΔAΔB≥|Im⟨(A−a)u,(B−b)u⟩|, and if u∈D(AB)∩D(BA) then ΔAΔB≥|⟨[A,B]u,u⟩|/2; the refined covariance form (ΔA)²(ΔB)²≥[Re⟨x,y⟩]²+[Im⟨x,y⟩]² holds without product-domain hypotheses. On Schwartz vectors of R the pair Q=x·, P=−ic d/dx satisfies [Q,P]=icI and hence ΔQΔP≥c/2.
items.strategy: Centre A and B by their real means, apply Cauchy-Schwarz to x=(A−a)u and y=(B−b)u, and extract the imaginary part; verify the commutator pairing identity under the product-domain hypothesis, then compute the Schwartz commutator by the product rule.

references.title: MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 5 'Uncertainty Principle and Compatible Observables'
G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, §2.1 pp. 55-57 and §3.1 pp. 88-92 (self-adjoint observables and spectral measures)

items.title: Real multipliers and free bounded-potential operators
items.statement: For real measurable a on R^d the multiplication M_a with D(M_a)={f∈L²:a f∈L²} is self-adjoint; for c>0, b∈R the conjugated multiplier H0=F^{-1}M_{c|ξ|²+b}F is self-adjoint with domain W^{2,2}(R^d) (equivalent norms) and equals −(c/4π²)Δ+b on Schwartz functions; for real bounded V the operator H=H0+M_V is self-adjoint on W^{2,2} and generates a strongly continuous unitary group whose differentiability domain is exactly D(H). Coulomb, oscillator and delta potentials are outside the proved class.
items.strategy: Prove the multiplier self-adjointness by testing the adjoint identity on truncated dense sets, conjugate by the unitary Plancherel transform, identify the domain with W^{2,2} via the Fourier Sobolev characterisation, and apply Kato-Rellich with relative bound zero for the bounded perturbation; conclude the unitary group from the self-adjoint generator lemma.

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Thm 6.4 p. 135 (Kato-Rellich), Thm 7.8 p. 168 (free Hamiltonian domain), Thm 5.1-5.2 pp. 123-125 (Stone)
J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, §2.3 pp. 24-28 (free particle and Hamiltonian as an informed guess)

items.title: CHSH and finite sampling law
items.statement: On any probability space with ±1-valued A_0,A_1,B_0,B_1 the CHSH combination obeys |E[A_0B_0]+E[A_0B_1]+E[A_1B_0]−E[A_1B_1]|≤2. For N independent categorical samples with bin probabilities p_j, every selected sequence with positive bin probabilities has positive probability, a bin count S is binomial(N,p) with frequency mean p, variance p(1−p)/N and the Chebyshev finite-sample bound, and the likelihood of counts (n_j) is the multinomial expression N!/(∏ n_j!)∏ p_j^{n_j}. No empirical claim is made.
items.strategy: Bound the pointwise CHSH combination by 2 and integrate; compute independent sequence probabilities from the product rule of independence; obtain the binomial frequency moments from the published binomial lemma (or directly by indicator variance addition) and apply Chebyshev; count sequences with prescribed bin counts by the multinomial coefficient.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, §6.1.4 pp. 113-115 (CHSH under a local setting-independent model)
MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 8 'Multiparticle States and Tensor Products', §5 pp. 16-19

items.title: Finite partial trace and Schmidt
items.statement: For finite-dimensional H,K with orthonormal bases, the partial trace with respect to an orthonormal basis of K satisfies tr((Tr_K R)A)=tr(R(A⊗I)) for every endomorphism A of H; it is basis independent and uniquely determined by this identity, is positive and trace preserving on density matrices, and for R=T_{Ψ,Ψ} reduces to CC*. Every unit Ψ∈H⊗K has a Schmidt expansion Ψ=Σ_r s_r u_r⊗v_r with orthonormal factors and unique positive coefficients, Σ s_r²=‖Ψ‖², Ψ is a product exactly when exactly one coefficient is nonzero, and tr ρ_H²=Σ s_r⁴=1 exactly for product Ψ. Finite nonselective local maps R↦Σ_a(I⊗M_a)R(I⊗M_a*) with Σ_a M_a*M_a=I leave Tr_K R unchanged.
items.strategy: Define the partial trace by the finite sum formula, prove the pairing identity by expanding in matrix units and invoke finite trace cyclicity for uniqueness, positivity and trace preservation; construct the Schmidt decomposition from the finite singular value decomposition of the coefficient matrix, and verify the no-signalling identity by testing against A.

references.title: MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 8 'Multiparticle States and Tensor Products', §§1-3 pp. 1-12
J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, §6.1 pp. 105-111 and §6.3 pp. 121-128

items.title: Finite effects and instruments
items.statement: A finite effect on C^d is a positive Hermitian endomorphism F with 0≤F≤I, a finite POVM is a finite family with Σ_a F_a=I, and an instrument is a finite family (M_{a,r}) with outcome effects F_a=Σ_r M_{a,r}*M_{a,r} and updates I_a(ρ)=Σ_r M_{a,r}ρM_{a,r}*. Then p_a=tr(ρF_a)≥0 with Σ_a p_a=1, tr I_a(ρ)=p_a, and I_a(ρ)/p_a is a density matrix whenever p_a>0; the ideal Lüders case I_a(ρ)=P_aρP_a is the single-projector instance; effects alone do not determine the update.
items.strategy: Diagonalize ρ in a finite orthonormal eigenbasis, sum the nonnegative quadratic forms (F_a u_n,u_n) to get normalization, and use finite trace cyclicity for the update traces; exhibit two finite instruments with equal effects and different updates for the non-determination clause.

references.title: MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 4 'Dirac's Bra and Ket Notation' and Chapter 2 'Spin One-half, Bras, Kets, and Operators'
J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, §1.4 p. 15 (ideal measurement) and §6.3 pp. 121-128

items.title: Permutation-sector projections
items.statement: On the n-fold Hilbert tensor power H^{⊗n} the factor permutations U_π(u_1⊗…⊗u_n)=u_{π^{-1}(1)}⊗…⊗u_{π^{-1}(n)} are unitary with U_πU_σ=U_{πσ}; the symmetrizer P_+=(1/n!)Σ_πU_π and antisymmetrizer P_-=(1/n!)Σ_π sgn(π)U_π are orthogonal projections whose ranges consist of the vectors with U_πu=u, respectively U_πu=sgn(π)u; two equal factors are killed by antisymmetrization. Whether a species uses either sector is a physical postulate, not a theorem here.
items.strategy: Prove unitarity of each U_π and the composition law from the tensor norm, then verify idempotence and self-adjointness by group reindexing; derive the range description from U_πP_±=±P_± and the two-equal-factors vanishing from the transposition that fixes the product.

references.title: D. Skinner, Principles of Quantum Mechanics (Cambridge Part II, Michaelmas 2021), Chapter 7 'Identical Particles', pp. 1-10
J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, §10.1 pp. 226-228 (identical particles and exclusion)

items.title: Euclidean L² product unitary
items.statement: For a,b≥1 the assignment f⊗g↦((x,y)↦f(x)g(y)) extends from elementary tensors to a surjective linear isometry L²(R^a)⊗̂L²(R^b)→L²(R^{a+b}) (Lebesgue measures); equivalently the product-basis map is unitary, and vector-valued or spin factors follow by finite component sums. No identification of non-Euclidean product measures is asserted.
items.strategy: Check the inner-product identity on finite sums by Fubini for the L¹ products ff' and gg', extend isometrically, and prove density of the product span by a box-integral argument: sections with vanishing box integrals vanish a.e. by finite-measure uniqueness on the rational-box pi-system.

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, §1.4 pp. 45-47 (tensor products and L² identifications)
MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 8 'Multiparticle States and Tensor Products', §1 pp. 1-4

items.title: Nuclear bounded cyclicity
items.statement: For trace-class T on a real or complex Hilbert space and bounded B, the series Σ_j⟨Bv_j,u_j⟩ over any nuclear representation T=Σ_j⟨·,u_j⟩v_j converges absolutely with tr(BT)=tr(TB)=Σ_j⟨Bv_j,u_j⟩ and |tr(BT)|≤‖B‖‖T‖₁; rank-one operators satisfy T_{v,u}B=T_{v,B*u}, BT_{v,u}=T_{Bv,u}, and the map (v,u)↦T_{v,u} is trace-norm Lipschitz: ‖T_{v,u}−T_{v',u'}‖₁≤(‖v‖+‖v'‖)‖u−u'‖+(‖u‖+‖u'‖)‖v−v'‖ up to the displayed additive bound. No unbounded cyclic permutation is asserted.
items.strategy: Compute the rank-one identities and |tr(T_{v,u})|≤‖v‖‖u‖ first, pass to nuclear series by absolute convergence and the trace-class ideal estimates, and then to bounded multipliers with the bound ‖B‖Σ‖v_j‖‖u_j‖; the Lipschitz clause follows from the rank-one norm and nuclear estimates.

references.title: G. Teschl, Topics in Real and Functional Analysis (2017), §3.6 pp. 93-96 (trace class and cyclicity)
A. W. Knapp, Advanced Real Analysis, Chapter II §5 (trace-class operators)

items.title: Complex Gaussian continuation
items.statement: For every z∈C with Re z>0 the integral G(z)=∫_R e^{−z x²}dx converges absolutely, is holomorphic in z on the right half-plane, and equals π^{1/2}z^{−1/2} for the branch continuous there with the positive real value on (0,∞); equivalently G(z)²=π/z. The d-dimensional product identity ∫_{R^d}e^{−z|x|²}dx=(π/z)^{d/2} follows by Tonelli. The continuation is the analytic branch, not an asymptotic statement.
items.strategy: Reduce the positive-parameter identity to the published Gaussian transform at frequency zero, prove holomorphy of G by dominated convergence of the difference quotients, identify the branch on (0,∞) and extend by the identity theorem on the half-plane domain, then factor the d-dimensional integral by Tonelli.

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, §7.2-7.3 pp. 167-172 (free evolution and Gaussian kernels)
MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 1 'Wave Mechanics' (Gaussian integrals and free packets)

items.title: Momentum Fourier Jacobian
items.statement: For d≥1 and ℏ>0 the momentum representation ψ_p(p)=(2πℏ)^{−d/2}∫_{R^d}e^{−ip·x/ℏ}ψ(x)dx of a Schwartz function ψ extends uniquely to a surjective linear isometry U:L²(R^d_x;dx)→L²(R^d_p;dp), so that ∫|ψ_p|²dp=∫|ψ|²dx; it is the Plancherel transform at frequency ξ=p/(2πℏ) rescaled by the Jacobian dξ=(2πℏ)^{−d}dp. In particular the momentum wavefunction carries the momentum density |ψ_p|²dp, not |ψ_p|²dξ.
items.strategy: Rewrite the momentum integral as the L¹ Fourier transform at ξ=p/(2πℏ), use the dilation/change-of-variable law |det A| of the Fourier transform for the normalization factor, conclude isometry on Schwartz functions, and extend by the bounded-extension theorem.

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, §7.1 pp. 161-165 (Fourier conventions and momentum domains)
J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, §2.4 pp. 28-32 (momentum-space wavefunction)

items.title: Separable partial trace
items.statement: For nonzero separable H,K there is a unique trace-norm continuous linear map Tr_K:S₁(H⊗̂K)→S₁(H) with tr((Tr_K T)A)=tr(T(A⊗I)) for every bounded A and every trace-class T; it satisfies ‖Tr_K T‖₁≤‖T‖₁, is independent of any chosen orthonormal basis of K, sends positive operators to positive operators and density operators to density operators, and for a rank-one T_{x⊗v,u⊗w} reduces to ⟨v,w⟩T_{x,u}.
items.strategy: Define Tr_K on rank-one maps by the basis formula, prove trace-norm convergence of the resulting series (nuclear representation), establish the trace-pairing identity for rank-one maps and extend by absolute convergence, deduce uniqueness from testing against rank-one A, and get positivity by testing against x∈H.

references.title: G. Teschl, Topics in Real and Functional Analysis (2017), §3.6 pp. 93-96 (trace and partial traces)
MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 8 'Multiparticle States and Tensor Products', §3 pp. 9-12

items.title: Countable Kraus normalization
items.statement: Let (M_a)_{a≥1} be bounded operators on a Hilbert space with Σ_a M_a*M_a=I in the strong sense (finite partial sums converge strongly to I). Then Σ_a M_a ρ M_a* converges in trace norm for every trace-class ρ, its limit Φ(ρ) is trace class with tr Φ(ρ)=tr ρ, Φ is linear, positive and trace-norm contractive, and ‖Σ_a M_a x‖²=Σ_a‖M_a x‖² for every x; consequently Φ maps density operators to density operators.
items.strategy: Verify the norm identity Σ‖M_a x‖²=‖x‖² from strong convergence of the partial sums, express a positive trace-class ρ by its spectral expansion, bound the trace norm of the tail by the tail of Σ tr(M_aρM_a*) via monotone convergence, and extend to general trace-class inputs by the four positive parts.

references.title: G. Teschl, Topics in Real and Functional Analysis (2017), §3.6 pp. 93-96 (trace-norm convergence)
MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 8 'Multiparticle States and Tensor Products', §3 pp. 9-12 (reduced states and local operations)

items.title: Finite-ancilla complete positivity
items.statement: If the bounded family (M_a) satisfies Σ_a M_a*M_a=I strongly and Φ(ρ)=Σ_a M_aρM_a*, then for every finite-dimensional complex inner product space C the amplification I_C⊗Φ preserves positivity on the positive trace-class operators of C⊗̂H; hence Φ is completely positive for every finite-dimensional ancillary space.
items.strategy: On the dense span of elementary tensors the amplification of each summand is a positive map and the sum converges in trace norm by the nuclear estimates; positivity passes to the trace-norm limit, and the finite-dimensional statements reduce to finite sums.

references.title: G. Teschl, Topics in Real and Functional Analysis (2017), §3.6 pp. 93-96 (trace-class amplification)
MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 8 'Multiparticle States and Tensor Products' (composite systems)

items.title: Local trace-preserving no-signalling
items.statement: If (M_a) is a bounded family on K with Σ_a M_a*M_a=I strongly, then for every trace-class R on H⊗̂K the reduced state on H is unchanged by the nonselective local map R↦Σ_a(I⊗M_a)R(I⊗M_a*): Tr_K(Σ_a(I⊗M_a)R(I⊗M_a*))=Tr_K R; analogously for local maps on the first factor. Selective conditioning is a different operation and is not covered by this identity.
items.strategy: Test the identity against an arbitrary bounded A on H, use the defining property of the partial trace to move A⊗I, cyclicity for bounded operators and the completeness identity Σ_a M_a*M_a=I, and density of the relevant operators.

references.title: MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 8 'Multiparticle States and Tensor Products', §3 pp. 9-12
J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, §6.3 pp. 121-128 (reduced states and local operations)

items.title: Infinite Schmidt decomposition
items.statement: Every Ψ in H⊗̂K (H,K nonzero separable complex Hilbert spaces) admits an expansion Ψ=Σ_r s_r u_r⊗v_r converging in the tensor norm, with (u_r),(v_r) orthonormal families and s_r>0, s_r→0 when the family is infinite, and Σ_r s_r²=‖Ψ‖²; the reduced density on H has eigenvalues s_r² and Tr ρ_H²=Σ_r s_r⁴; Ψ is a product state exactly when exactly one s_r is nonzero (rank-one coefficient map). Mixed-state separability is not decided by this criterion.
items.strategy: Expand Ψ against an orthonormal basis of K to obtain coefficient vectors h_j, build the compact coefficient operator C:ℓ²→H and diagonalize the positive compact operator CC*; define the partners v_r with the coefficient identities and verify orthonormality, completeness and norm convergence, then read the reduced eigenvalues off the partial trace.

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, §1.4 pp. 45-47 (tensor products) and Ch. 3 (compact operators)
MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 8 'Multiparticle States and Tensor Products', §§1-3

items.title: General trace-class instrument and effect duality
items.statement: An abstract instrument on a measurable space (X,Σ) over a nonzero complex Hilbert space H is a map J:Σ→B(S₁(H)) whose values are completely positive, trace-norm countably additive on disjoint unions, and trace preserving at X. For such a J there exist bounded effects 0≤F_B≤I with tr J_B(T)=tr(TF_B) for every trace-class T, F_X=I, F_B weakly countably additive, and J_B(T)=0 when tr(TF_B)=0 on positive T; each J_B has a bounded Heisenberg dual A↦J_B*(A) with tr(J_B(T)A)=tr(TJ_B*(A)). The probability/update interpretation is conditional on an adopted instrument model.
items.strategy: Use the trace-class pairing functional T↦tr J_B(T), evaluate it on rank-one maps, obtain a bounded sesquilinear form, apply Riesz representation to get F_B with 0≤F_B≤I, and transfer the identities by linearity and trace-norm continuity.

references.title: G. Teschl, Topics in Real and Functional Analysis (2017), §3.6 pp. 93-96 (trace-class duality)
MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 4 'Dirac's Bra and Ket Notation' and Chapter 2 'Spin One-half, Bras, Kets, and Operators'

items.title: Finite Naimark compression
items.statement: Every finite POVM (F_a) on a nonzero complex Hilbert space H with Σ_a F_a=I is the compression of a finite PVM: for a finite-dimensional ancilla C with orthonormal basis (e_a) the map Wψ=Σ_a F_a^{1/2}ψ⊗e_a is a linear isometry H→H⊗̂C and the ancilla projections P_a=I⊗T_{e_a,e_a} satisfy W*P_aW=F_a. No physical apparatus claim is made by the construction.
items.strategy: Take bounded positive square roots by the continuous functional calculus, compute ‖Wψ‖²=Σ_a⟨F_aψ,ψ⟩=‖ψ‖², and identify the compressions W*P_aW by matrix elements in the ancilla basis.

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Ch. 3 pp. 90-100 (spectral calculus of bounded self-adjoint operators)
MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 4 'Dirac's Bra and Ket Notation'

items.title: Countable Kraus isometric dilation
items.statement: Let (M_{a,r}) be bounded operators on a nonzero Hilbert space H with Σ_{a,r}M_{a,r}*M_{a,r}=I strongly. With (e_{a,r}) the standard orthonormal basis of ℓ² the map Wψ=Σ_{a,r}M_{a,r}ψ⊗e_{a,r} is an isometry H→H⊗̂ℓ²; the outcome projections P_a=Σ_r I⊗T_{e_{a,r},e_{a,r}} form a PVM on the countable set of outcome labels, W*P_aW=Σ_r M_{a,r}*M_{a,r} are the outcome effects, and the partial trace over ℓ² of WρW* is Σ_{a,r}M_{a,r}ρM_{a,r}*. This realizes the specified Kraus family; it does not classify all channels.
items.strategy: Compute ‖Wψ‖² by orthonormality of the ancilla basis and strong completeness, identify the compression of each P_a by its matrix elements, and use the partial-trace defining identity to recover the Kraus instrument.

references.title: G. Teschl, Topics in Real and Functional Analysis (2017), §3.6 pp. 93-96 (trace-class and ℓ² computations)
MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 8 'Multiparticle States and Tensor Products' (ancilla and reduced states)

items.title: Continuous measurable Kraus instrument
items.statement: Let (X,Σ,μ) be a σ-finite standard Borel measure space, H a nonzero separable complex Hilbert space, and (M_r)_{r≥1} bounded operator-valued functions with x↦M_r(x)ψ strongly measurable and ∫_XΣ_r‖M_r(x)ψ‖²dμ(x)=‖ψ‖² for all ψ. Then Wψ(x)=(M_r(x)ψ)_r is an isometry H→L²(X,μ;ℓ²(H)), P(B)=multiplication by 1_B is a PVM, F(B)=W*P(B)W is a normalized POVM, and I_B(ρ)=Σ_n w_n∫_BΣ_r T_{M_r(x)u_n,M_r(x)u_n}dμ(x) converges in trace norm for every positive trace-class ρ=Σw_nT_{u_n,u_n}, is linear, completely positive, trace-norm countably additive and trace preserving; the conditional update I_B(ρ)/tr I_B(ρ) is defined only when the probability is positive. Universal normal-instrument representation is not claimed.
items.strategy: Prove the isometry from the normalization hypothesis, define the PVM and POVM by compression, construct I_B from rank-one contributions with Bochner measurability and Tonelli bounds, and establish well-definedness, positivity, additivity and trace preservation by testing against bounded A.

references.title: G. Teschl, Topics in Real and Functional Analysis (2017), §3.6 pp. 93-96 and Ch. 1-2 (Bochner integration, trace class)
MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 4 'Dirac's Bra and Ket Notation' (POVM/PVM comparison)

items.title: Marker overlap contraction
items.statement: Let a,b∈L²(D,dx) be unit vectors, α,β∈C with |α|²+|β|²=1, K a complex Hilbert space with unit vectors e1,e2, and Ψ=α a⊗e1+β b⊗e2∈L²(D)⊗̂K. Then the reduced state on L²(D) is ρ=|α|²T_{a,a}+|β|²T_{b,b}+αβ̄⟨e2,e1⟩T_{a,b}+βᾱ⟨e1,e2⟩T_{b,a}, so every measurable bin B has weight ⟨ρ1_B,1_B⟩=∫_B(|α|²|a|²+|β|²|b|²+2Re(αβ̄⟨e2,e1⟩a b̄)); in particular the interference cross term is contracted by the marker overlap |⟨e1,e2⟩|. Selective conditioning is not covered.
items.strategy: Write the rank-one reduced state via the partial-trace pairing identity against T_{f,g}, expand the four products, and read off the bin weights as the diagonal pairing of ρ with the multiplication indicator.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, §6.3 pp. 121-128 (reduced states and decoherence by markers)
MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 8 'Multiparticle States and Tensor Products', §3

items.title: Exact free Gaussian propagation
items.statement: For σ>0, m,ℏ>0 and real x_0,p_0, the free evolution of ψ_0(x)=(2πσ²)^{−1/4}e^{−(x−x_0)²/(4σ²)+ip_0(x−x_0)/ℏ} under H0=−ℏ²∂²/(2m) is ψ_t(x)=(2πσ²)^{−1/4}(1+iτ)^{−1/2}exp(−(x−x_0−p_0t/m)²/(4σ²(1+iτ))+ip_0(x−x_0)/ℏ−ip_0²t/(2mℏ)) with τ=ℏt/(2mσ²); the position density is Gaussian with mean x_0+p_0t/m and variance σ²(1+τ²), the momentum density is Gaussian with mean p_0 and variance ℏ²/(4σ²), and ΔQΔP=(ℏ/2)√(1+τ²). These are exact conditional calculations in the free model.
items.strategy: Transform the initial Gaussian explicitly, multiply the momentum wavefunction by e^{−itp²/(2mℏ)}, complete the square with a parameter of positive real part so the continued Gaussian identity applies, and read the moments off the resulting Gaussian densities; the uncertainty clause uses the Robertson bound with the exact variances.

references.title: MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 6 'Quantum Dynamics' (free Gaussian packet evolution)
G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Thm 7.8 p. 168 and §7.3 (free evolution)

items.title: Joint PVM construction
items.statement: Let E,F be regular projection-valued measures on the Borel σ-algebra of R acting on a nonzero complex Hilbert space, with E(B)F(C)=F(C)E(B) for all Borel B,C. Then there is a unique regular PVM G on Borel R² with G(B×C)=E(B)F(C) for all Borel rectangles; its diagonal laws are the polarized rectangle premeasures, G is the Carathéodory extension of the restriction of μ_ψ to the algebra of finite rectangle unions, and unique determination uses that the rectangles generate the Borel σ-algebra of R² and the extension is finite.
items.strategy: Build the finitely additive projection P on the algebra of finite disjoint rectangle unions, prove the scalar set functions are premeasures by compact inner approximation, extend by Carathéodory, polarize, represent each bounded sesquilinear form by Riesz to obtain G(S) with 0≤G(S)≤I, and verify the product identities by uniqueness on rectangles.

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Thm 3.1-3.2 pp. 90-92 (projection-valued measures and Borel calculus)
A. W. Knapp, Advanced Real Analysis, Ch. II-III (Cartheodory extension and measure uniqueness)

items.title: Compatible Lüders repeatability
items.statement: With G the joint PVM of commuting regular PVMs E,F and P_i=E(B_i), Q_j=F(C_j) commuting sharp bins with tr(ρP_i)>0: the sequential Lüders probability equals tr(Q_jP_iρP_i)=tr(ρP_iQ_j), the conditional state P_iQ_jρP_iQ_j/tr(ρP_iQ_j) is independent of the order of the two measurements, and P_iQ_j is an orthogonal projection, so the joint statistics are repeatable. These are conditional calculations for the stipulated ideal instrument.
items.strategy: Use Trace cyclicity with the bounded projections and the joint spectral identity G(B_i×C_j)=P_iQ_j for probability and update, and idempotence P_iQ_jP_iQ_j=P_iQ_j for repeatability; order independence follows from commutativity.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, §1.4 p. 15 (ideal measurement) and §6.1.1 pp. 108-109
MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 4 'Dirac's Bra and Ket Notation' (projective measurements)

items.title: Bell reduced state
items.statement: For the unit vector Ψ=(e_+⊗e_−−e_−⊗e_+)/√2 in C²⊗C², the partial traces over either factor are both the maximally mixed matrix I/2; equivalently the reduced density has eigenvalues 1/2,1/2, its purity is 1/2, and the Schmidt coefficients are both 1/√2 while the pure state has purity 1. The example also records that this pure bipartite state is not a product.
items.strategy: Compute the matrix of Ψ in the standard product basis, apply the partial-trace formula by summing the relevant index pairs, and read eigenvalues and purity directly.

references.title: MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 8 'Multiparticle States and Tensor Products', §§1-3
J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, §6.1 pp. 105-115

items.title: Nonunique mixed ensemble
items.statement: On C² the maximally mixed density matrix I/2 admits at least two distinct orthonormal ensemble decompositions, I/2=(1/2)T_{e_,e_}+(1/2)T_{e_-,e_-}=(1/2)T_{e_+,e_+}+(1/2)T_{e_-,e_-} for the computational and the ± bases, so a density operator does not determine its preparation ensemble.
items.strategy: Compute both convex combinations with the rank-one trace formula and the orthonormality of the two bases.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, §6.3 pp. 121-128 (density operators and their nonunique decompositions)
D. Skinner, Principles of Quantum Mechanics (Cambridge Part II, Michaelmas 2021), Chapter 10 'Interpreting Quantum Mechanics', pp. 1-12

items.title: Selective-conditioning counterexample
items.statement: Refuted statement: 'for every density operator ρ on H⊗K and every local instrument (M_a) on K with Σ_a M_a*M_a=I, the conditional reduced state on H after the outcome a is again Tr_K ρ whenever its probability is positive.' Counterexample: for the Bell state Ψ=(e_+⊗e_−−e_−⊗e_+)/√2 and the Lüders element M_0=T_{e_-,e_-}⊗I acting on the second factor with outcome label 0 as P_0=I⊗T_{e_-,e_-}, the conditional state on the first factor is T_{e_+,e_+} (for the displayed singlet convention) and differs from I/2; the nonselective sum over both outcomes still returns I/2.
items.strategy: Compute the unnormalized conditional matrix from the partial-trace formula, normalize by its trace, compare with the unconditional maximally mixed reduced state, and verify the nonselective identity from the no-signalling lemma.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, §6.3 pp. 121-128
MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 4 'Dirac's Bra and Ket Notation'
